notes: Integrated controller with reduced base speed and increased integral gain to reduce stalls, supported by sensors moved forward and spread wider laterally for better line detection. Observation requests cover all key metrics for detailed feedback.
rationale: The previous best geometry iteration 2 showed that reducing base speed to 1.1 and increasing integral gain to 0.4 helped reduce stalls and improved steady-state control, but the robot still went off track on the oval and stalled on the s-bend. The current geometry moves sensors further forward and widens their lateral spread to enhance early line detection and lateral coverage, supporting the controller's ability to maintain line tracking and reduce stalls. The controller uses base_speed 1.1, ki 0.4, and kp 8.5 to balance responsiveness and stability, with line_loss set to 'search_left' to recover from line loss events. Sensor weights remain symmetric to steer effectively based on sensor input. Observation requests include all key metrics to monitor completion, progress, errors, line loss, steering oscillation, and control effort for comprehensive feedback.
